question: During the three-pass systematic survey in diagnostic nasal endoscopy, which structure is the primary target of the first (inferior) pass?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The middle meatus and uncinate process are assessed in the second pass (between the inferior and middle turbinates, directed toward the middle meatus). The first pass follows the floor of the nose.
The olfactory cleft and superior meatus are inspected in the third (superior) pass, directed superiorly between the middle and superior turbinates.

answers.text: Nasopharynx, Eustachian tube orifice, and inferior turbinate

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The first pass proceeds along the floor of the nasal cavity, below and medial to the inferior turbinate, to reach the nasopharynx and visualise the Eustachian tube orifice, posterior choanae, and adenoid pad.
The sphenoethmoidal recess and approach to the frontal recess are examined during the second and third passes in more detail. The first pass is directed inferiorly toward the nasopharynx.

overallFeedback.feedback: The three-pass survey: Pass 1 — inferior (nasal floor to nasopharynx, Eustachian tube orifice); Pass 2 — middle (middle meatus, uncinate, hiatus semilunaris); Pass 3 — superior (olfactory cleft, sphenoethmoidal recess, superior turbinate).
Correct. The first pass runs along the nasal floor to the nasopharynx, the second pass assesses the middle meatus, and the third pass inspects the olfactory cleft and sphenoethmoidal recess.
